Position Summary
Training Officers work in a dynamic vocational, education and training environment in which they have to adapt and be responsive to changes in national curriculum, the VET Quality Framework, technological developments and a diversity and breadth of client training demands.

The role of the Training Officer embraces the extent of the learning process from program enquiry/advice through to assessing and determining the training requirements of clients, following onto managing the learning process for clients using a variety of training strategies including recognition of prior learning, recognition of current competencies, training delivery, workplace learning, delivery and assessment, formal assessment and reporting etc..  

The training Officer will have the vocational skills in the area that they are applying for with a minimum of three to five years’ experience in their chosen vocational area.

The Training Officer ideally would have at least have obtained the following competencies from the Training and Assessment Training Package or is able to demonstrate equivalent competencies. However if the candidate does not have these competencies or the full Training & Assessment Qualification they will agree to work with an accredited assessor until this qualification is achieved.

The Training Officer is expected to be innovative in responding effectively to the training demands of clients.  The Training Officer works in a wide variety of learning environments providing a range of flexible training and learning strategies to best meet the client needs including flexible delivery, workplace training and assessment, training room delivery, on line learning support etc.   

The Training Officer will be expected to be able to work effectively as a member of a team and be required to be involved in a range of course/program coordination and administration activities that support the effective operation of the company and the achievement of learning outcomes for participants.  

POSITION PARAMETERS
1.	SUPERVISION AND ACCOUNTABILITY The position reports to the Manager and may work in a number of program areas. 
2.	LOCATION Training Staff are required to work on site or at a designated training facility.  
3.	PARTICIPATION ON COMMITTEES Training Officers are required to attend program meetings and team meetings, or other external committees as required.

Duty Statement
1.	Develop and manage the learning process for participants. 
2.	Train in a range of subjects and programs in a variety of learning modes at locations specified by the Manager. (See Attachment 1 for position details)
3.	Prepare quality learning and assessment resources within the context of established curriculum, training packages under the national framework, competency standards, the diversity of students and client’s requirements. Unless otherwise agreed with the Training Officer, Intellectual Property in all material developed or produced shall remain within Industry Training & Workplace Services.
4.	Participate as a member of a team on a range of tasks including curriculum and program development, program delivery, professional development, marketing activities and administrative and operational functions.
5.	Undertake, where required, course coordination and a range of planning tasks relevant to the delivery of quality courses.
6.	Provide support and advice to participants of diverse cultures, backgrounds and abilities and implement appropriate support strategies and/or learning programs and strategies as required.
7.	Undertake as required a range of participant support service tasks to ensure the effective operation of the Company, for example participant selection, course advice, enrolment and telephone enquiry support.
8.	Research, adapt and develop innovative learning practices and delivery options that enhance the Company's capacity to meet the demands of participants. 
9.	Manage the delivery of training services to industry, including workplace visits, assessing training needs, developing training plans and coordinating the effective delivery of programs.
10.	Participate in and contribute to the development and implementation of evaluation and continuous improvement processes across the Company.
11.	Undertake regular professional development to maintain and continuously improve individual professional and vocational competencies as a Training Officer.
12.	Comply with the quality assurance requirements of the Australian Quality Training Framework and the company’s Quality System.

SELECTION CRITERIA 
Qualifications
1.	The minimum training qualification is the Certificate IV in Training & Assessment or equivalent. 
2.	It is mandatory to have relevant vocational competence at or higher than the level being delivered or assessed through having qualifications and/or relevant industry experience. 
3.	Training Officers who do not hold the minimum or equivalent training qualification must undertake professional development to gain the training qualification within 12 months of commencement. In the interim, the training officer must agree to be mentored by a qualified Trainer who does hold the minimum or equivalent qualification

Training Excellence
1.	Demonstrated excellence in training, management of learning and assessment.
2.	Demonstrated experience in contributing to development of learning resources.
3.	 An understanding of current developments and innovative approaches in training.
4.	Demonstrated experience, or ability to, develop and conduct training programs suitable to the needs of industry.
5.	Demonstrated record of innovation in training and proven commitment to undertake regular professional development to maintain and continuously improve individual professional competence.

Communication Skills
1.	Proven ability to operate effectively as a member of a team.
2.	High level interpersonal and communication skills.
3.	Demonstrated ability to provide support and advice to students of diverse cultures, backgrounds and abilities.
Administration
1.	High level organisational skills
2.	Demonstrated experience in contributing to the overall functioning of the company including record keeping, course maintenance and quality improvement and ability to use all relevant technology.

Further Information
For further information please contact Toni Hoyle.
Telephone 90227100 or 0419 908 425

Heavy Diesel Plant Mechanic

Force Equipment, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Emeco Group, is seeking suitably experienced and qualified trades personnel to join our workshop teams. These teams are focused on the inspection, overhaul, rebuild, and repair of heavy mobile equipment components, supporting high-quality, reliable outcomes for our mining customers through industry-leading workshop facilities and systems.

Reporting to the Workshop Supervisor, you will be responsible for maintaining Force (and customer) equipment / machines ensuring availability / integrity, successful candidates will be responsible for: 

•	Focus on safe working environment and quality of workmanship. 
•	Major customer machine rebuilds carried out in the workshop
•	Ongoing repairs and maintenance of in-house and customer equipment
o	Maintenance and repairs on Caterpillar, Liebherr, Elphinstone, Sandvik, Atlas Copco - Epiroc, Hitachi and Komatsu mobile equipment    within budgets and time frames
o	Working with the Force Equipment customers to meet their company objectives; and
o	Quality control on all work performed. 

Your Skills and Experience:
•	Nationally recognised trade qualification
•	Experience with heavy earthmoving equipment
•	A strong commitment to safety
•	Good analytical and problem-solving skills with a solution focus
•	A keen eye for detail, presentation and craftsmanship; and
•	The ability to work as part of a cohesive team

We Offer 
•	Opportunity to grow and develop through training and future career opportunities
•	Competitive hourly rates
•	Variety of work; and
•	Permanent employment

About you
•	Australian recognised trade certificate
•	Demonstrated experience in servicing, repair and component change outs across a variety of mobile earthmoving equipment.

How to apply
Contact Lina on 0486 135 133 or Fololina.Filimaua@emecogroup.com for more info or click on 'Apply' and upload your CV today!
Emeco Group is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer - we encourage applicants who identify as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander to apply.

To learn more about Force job opportunities: https://forceequipment.com.au/careers

Location	Annerley, QLD, 4103
Full-Time	Immediate start
Reports to:	Centre Manager & ECT
Job Title	Early Childhood Teacher
Salary Range	$80,000 - $90,000 + Superannuation - depending on skill level.
Job Closes Date	30 Days  

About the Role
We are partnering with a highly respected early learning provider to find a nurturing and dedicated Early Childhood Teacher for their vibrant centre. This organisation is known for its commitment to nurturing children's growth through a play-based and holistic curriculum. With purpose-built facilities and a team of passionate educators, they create warm, inclusive environments where children feel safe, valued, and inspired to explore and learn.

Key Responsibilities
Curriculum & Pedagogy:
• Design, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive educational program aligned with the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and the service's philosophy.
• Employ intentional teaching strategies within a play-based learning environment to foster cognitive, social, and emotional development.
• Lead engaging learning experiences across key domains, including literacy, numeracy, creative arts, and physical activity.

Assessment & Documentation:
• Conduct detailed observations and use critical reflection to assess children's learning and progress against individual and group goals.
• Create rich and detailed portfolios and learning stories that make children's learning visible to families and colleagues.
• Use documented evidence to plan forward and ensure a dynamic, responsive curriculum.

Leadership & Mentorship:
• Provide guidance and support to other educators within the room, modelling best practices in early childhood teaching.
• Contribute to a collaborative culture of continuous improvement and reflective practice among the teaching team.

Family & Community Partnership:
• Build strong, respectful, and collaborative partnerships with families through formal and informal communication.
• Lead family-teacher meetings and discussions about child development and learning goals.
• Actively participate in community events and centre initiatives to strengthen community ties.

Compliance & Professionalism:
• Ensure all practices meet the National Quality Standard and relevant regulatory requirements.
• Maintain a safe, inclusive, and stimulating learning environment for all children.
• Engage in ongoing professional development and contribute to the service's quality improvement plan.

Skills & Experience
• A Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (or ACECQA-approved equivalent) is essential.
• A current and valid Victorian Institute of Teaching (VIT) Registration.
• Proven experience as an Early Childhood Teacher within a long day care or similar setting.
• Deep knowledge and practical application of the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and National Quality Standards (NQS).
• Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills for building relationships with children, families, and colleagues.
• Current First Aid, Asthma & Anaphylaxis Certification (HLTAID012).
• A valid Working with Children Check and National Police Check.
• Proof of up-to-date vaccination status as per service policy.

Why Apply?
This is more than a job - it's an opportunity to shape young lives in an environment that values educator wellbeing as much as child development. You'll receive:
• Above-award wages for qualified candidates
• Paid professional development opportunities
• Supportive leadership team with realistic expectations
• Purpose-built facilities with quality resources

If you're ready to make your mark in early childhood education with an organisation that values your expertise, we'd love to hear from you.

How to Apply:
Submit your resume and cover letter addressing your experience with the EYLF and your approach to play-based learning. Successful applicants will require valid working rights and must pass background checks.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.









Shape Digital Healthcare. Drive Innovation. Improve Lives. 












About the Department of Clinical Informatics 






The Department of Clinical Informatics is where healthcare and technology come together to transform patient care. 






Established in 2025, we bring together clinical, digital and innovation expertise to shape the future of healthcare across Monash Health. Our multidisciplinary team spans Nursing, Medical, Allied Health and Community Informatics, Digital Clinical Learning and Change, Artificial Intelligence, Consumer Informatics, User Experience and Clinical Coding. 






The Department is committed to building a high-performing team and improving patient outcomes through digital innovation, aligned with the Monash Health Strategic Plan and Digital & Data Plan. 






If you're passionate about innovation, collaboration and using technology to make a real difference in healthcare, this newly created full-time, ongoing role offers the chance to help shape the future from the ground up. 












About the Role 






This ground-breaking role is designed to enable our clinical teams to readily and safely transform patient care, using digital technologies. Intersecting with clinical practice, digital health, change management and workplace capability building, this is a rare opportunity to lead the transition of our clinicians, in all professional streams, to embrace the benefits of a digitally thinking workplace. 






Far from a "Business As Usual" role, this opportunity will suit individuals seeking to leverage strategic leadership and advice to engineer a significant change in the way we deliver patient care. Acknowledging the rapid rate of change in the digital space, you are not deterred by uncertainty. If appointed, you will relish the chance to apply your innovative thinking skills to build diverse, agile, high performing teams. 






As a key member of our Clinical Informatics leadership team, your success will be measured across three key result areas: 









Leadership of change of learning functions and practices 












Collaboration with Clinical Informatics and Digital and Information Division 












Stakeholder engagement and relationship development 









You'll appreciate that the collaborative nature of this role will see you working on site at least three days per week, with flexible working arrangements available. With accountability for the function across the whole of organisation, travel across Monash Health will be required. 












About You 






You have a keen understanding of informatics as well as demonstrated knowledge of adult learning principles. Described as visionary, you also have the ability to translate organisational objectives into practical and effective practices that advance care at the operational level. 






You are comfortable working with ambiguity. Your emotional intelligence equips you with the skills and strategies to navigate the challenges of change respectfully, professionally and sensitively, adapting your style to meet the needs of varying audiences. 






Our clinical teams are highly skilled, busy and saturated with information. Your job will be to enhance their Joy in Work through equipping them with a relevant, digitally-enabled approach that will see them continue to deliver consistently high standards of care in the community we serve. 



What you need 






Your ability to engage and influence effectively across a range of professional groups, pivoting seamlessly between clinical, technical and strategic perspectives, will be key to your success. 






To be considered for this role, you'll need to demonstrate: 









Deep clinical systems expertise and success leading enterprise change 












Strategic leadership of integrated change and learning functions to drive enterprise-wid digitatl transformation 












Intimate appreciation of transformation as it relates to building digital capability 












Expertise in adult learning, enabling success driving digital adoption and optimisation 












Awareness of digital architecture and how systems communicate, share, exchange and use data 












Detailed knowledge of clinical safety and risk management 












Data and information fluency 









Current Ahpra registration, a postgraduate qualification in Digital Health, Informatics, Learning-Education, Change Management and-or leadership are required. 












Why join Monash Health? 






This is more than a digital role-it's your chance to transform healthcare at scale. Working at the intersection of clinical care, technology and innovation, you'll help create smarter digital solutions that improve patient outcomes and support the clinicians who deliver them every day 












At Monash Health, you will: 









Lead a state-wide service with real impact 












Work within a values-driven, purpose-led organisation 












Be part of a connected network of clinical, academic and system leaders 












Help drive innovation, inclusion and better health outcomes 















We offer: 









The opportunity to make a real impact on patient experience 












A supportive, collaborative team environment 












Ongoing learning and development opportunities 












The chance to be part of Victoria's largest public health service













For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Anthony Pham, Deputy Chief Nursing and Midwifery Information Officer on 0435 968 584.

result.description:
Our client, a leading supplier within the construction and steel manufacturing industry, is seeking experienced Machine Operators to join their team in Bassendean! 
  This role is focused on processing reinforcing steel (rebar) used in concrete and masonry construction projects. You will operate specialised machinery to cut, bend, and shape rebar to customer specifications before preparing finished products for dispatch. 
  This role offers a Monday to Friday roster with the choice of either a day shift (5am until 1pm) or an afternoon shift (1pm until 9pm). 
     About the Role  
 Your duties will include: 
 
 Operating rebar processing machinery, including coil processing machines, guillotine cutters, and bending equipment 
 Cutting and shaping reinforcing steel to production requirements 
 Bundling, stacking, and securing finished products 
 Operating an overhead crane to move materials throughout the warehouse 
 Loading finished products onto trucks for dispatch 
 Following all site safety procedures and maintaining housekeeping standards 
 Working within a small, safety-focused team environment 
 
     What We're Looking For  
 To be successful in this role, you will have: 
 
 Previous machine operating experience within a manufacturing, production, warehouse, or industrial environment 
 Strong mechanical aptitude and confidence working around machinery 
 A proactive approach to workplace safety 
 A current driver's licence (essential) 
 Full work rights in Australia 
 
   Who we are  
 As one of Australia's largest employers, we work with great companies all around Australia and New Zealand to give you the best opportunities to work when and where you want to. 
 At Programmed, we are committed to creating a safe and inclusive environment which values and respects diverse styles, backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. 
 We welcome and encourage women, people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent and people from diverse backgrounds to apply.
